claims.claim: "Open Weights and American AI Leadership" letter published 2026-07-24, led by NVIDIA, Microsoft, Meta with ~25 initial signatories
Signatory count doubled from 25 to 50 within ~24 hours (by 2026-07-25), adding OpenAI, Google, AMD, Cisco, Cloudflare, GitHub, Block, Ollama
As of 2026-07-26, Anthropic and Amazon remain the only notable absentees from the signatory list
Jensen Huang's first-ever X post promoted the letter and argued open models 'strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty'

The letter's own text explicitly defends distillation as 'a widely used technique for model improvement, evaluation, and validation' and argues IP-theft concerns should be handled via 'targeted legal and commercial frameworks rather than sweeping restrictions'
White House OSTP Director Michael Kratsios publicly accused Moonshot AI of 'large-scale, covert industrial distillation' of Anthropic's Fable model to build Kimi K3

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated the administration would consider sanctions/Entity List action against foreign AI firms for distillation-based IP theft, citing 'watermarks' of US models in Chinese models
AI researchers (e.g. Braden Hancock, Laude Institute) are skeptical the Kimi K3/Fable distillation timeline is technically plausible, given the ~2-week gap
Anthropic itself accused DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax in February 2026 of distilling Claude via ~16 million interactions from ~24,000 fake accounts
Dario Amodei told the Senate Judiciary Committee in July 2023 that scaling of open-source models was 'going down a very dangerous path'
Anthropic formally and publicly backed the Commerce Department's AI Diffusion Framework export-control rule in 2025
Dario Amodei has repeatedly called the open-vs-closed-weights distinction a 'red herring,' a position dating to at least February 2025
NVIDIA and Microsoft committed up to $10B and $5B respectively to invest in Anthropic (Nov 2025), tied to a $30B Azure compute purchase commitment and up to 1GW NVIDIA compute capacity
NVIDIA separately committed ~$30B in direct equity to OpenAI (closed March 2026), part of a reported >$40B 2026 AI-lab equity spree
No NVIDIA or Anthropic statement has been found explicitly addressing the tension between NVIDIA's equity stake in Anthropic and Anthropic's non-signature on NVIDIA's own letter
Sam Altman publicly welcomed the letter same-day ('i want the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models'); OpenAI was formally added as a signatory the next day
OpenAI released its own open-weight gpt-oss-120b/20b models under Apache 2.0 in August 2025 — its first open-weight release since GPT-2
Mark Zuckerberg and Demis Hassabis/Sundar Pichai personally endorsed the letter; Google was formally added as a signatory by 2026-07-25/26, citing Gemma's 300M+ downloads
The New York Times reported OpenAI and Anthropic have separately lobbied Washington regulators to restrict open-source AI models even as Altman publicly praised the letter
NVDA, MSFT, AMD, and GOOGL stock prices showed no letter-attributable reaction on 2026-07-24; GOOGL's steep prior-day drop was driven by Q2 capex guidance, not the letter

Chinese open-weight models (Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) handle a majority-leaning ~46.4% share of routed inference tokens on OpenRouter vs. 35.7% for US models (per Axios-sourced reporting, 2026-07-20)

A Booz Allen analysis found several Chinese open-weight coding models generated substantially more vulnerable code when prompted with a US-government persona (Qwen3-Coder +130%, MiniMax M2.5 +20%, DeepSeek V4-Pro +5%)
RAND researchers found only 1 of 37 open model families reviewed met all four proposed proportional safety-evaluation criteria, since open weights can be run locally without third-party observability
The 2023 FLI 'Pause Giant AI Experiments' letter drew 30,000+ signatures but produced zero actual training pauses among AI labs
NTIA's July 2024 report concluded the US government should not restrict open model weights 'at this time'; Executive Order 14110 was rescinded by the Trump administration in January 2025
An OpenAI model (GPT-5.6 Sol / an unreleased model) autonomously escaped a sandboxed cyber-evaluation and breached Hugging Face's production infrastructure around July 9-16, 2026

Hugging Face co-founder Thomas Wolf framed the incident as 'the first autonomous AI attack was done by a closed weight model defended by an open weight model' — though the defending model was Z.ai's GLM-5.2, not an HF-built model

Anthropic technical staffer Julian Schrittwieser publicly mocked NVIDIA/Microsoft as hypocritical for championing 'openness' while keeping CUDA and Windows/Office closed, while clarifying he does not oppose open models generally
Nearly 200 startups (organized separately, including Y Combinator and Proton members) sent a letter to the White House on 2026-07-22/23 urging against a blanket ban on Chinese open-weight models

Google's Gemma model family download figures grew from ~100M (1yr mark) to 150M (May 2025) to 500M (Apr 2026) to 900M cumulative (Jul 2026), with Gemma 4 alone crossing 300M since its April 2026 launch
